summary: Nine compute-bound experiments completed in 146.8 minutes. The 69.0-minute bounded constraint-elimination prototype was the longest; the supplied evidence does not identify its costly phase, and the locked compute-task GPU-idle classification is false.
bottlenecks_identified: Runtime was concentrated in the 69.0-minute bounded constraint-elimination prototype and the 35.3-minute and 34.68-minute compute-bound tasks.
The timing data has no phase breakdown, so it cannot explain why the longest compute-bound experiments took as long as they did.
The GPU report is a point-in-time snapshot rather than task-window telemetry, so it cannot establish sustained compute efficiency.
No model-count or runner-dispatch evidence is supplied, so no missed DualGPURunner dispatch can be established.
improvements_suggested: Add phase timers and resumable checkpoints to long compute paths so the next retrospective can isolate expensive stages and interrupted work need not replay completed stages.
Join GPU utilization, memory, process identity, and cleanup events to each experiment's start and stop window.
Record model count, runner choice, and device assignment at launch; use DualGPURunner only when two or more models are actually loaded in parallel.
Emit one machine-readable execution receipt that combines phase timing, checkpoint status, accelerator telemetry, and dispatch metadata.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Instrument phase boundaries and checkpoint completion in the longest compute paths.
Capture task-scoped GPU and process-lifecycle telemetry, including post-task memory release.
Log model cardinality and runner/device selection, with dual-device dispatch limited to eligible parallel multi-model work.
meta_reflection: The evidence supports elapsed-time ranking but not causal attribution. A zero savings estimate is retained because no measured counterfactual quantifies the benefit of any proposed change.
